From: Tom Wu <tom.wu@edgeplay.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Danielle Reyes <danielle@finops.io>
Date: 2027-06-27T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up — TTFT + streaming questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo earlier — nice to see the SDK and the realtime metrics. A few quick clarifications from our side so we can align with infra: 

- TTFT expectations: we need p95 time-to-first-token for short prompts (<= 64 tokens) to be <= 150ms in our US region under steady concurrency of 50 concurrent chat sessions. Can Redwood hit that with the hosted offering or would we need Dedicated?
- Streaming mode: we prefer SSE for browser clients but have a small set of mobile clients that will use WebSocket. Any meaningful delta in TTFT between SSE and WS in practice?
- Chunk cadence: our UX team pushes small frequent updates (roughly 100–200ms cadence). Will that increase costs dramatically compared to batching at 300–400ms?
- Fallbacks: if the model variant is quantized to reduce cost, what delta should we expect in TTFT and token quality?

Attached a short payload sample and our SLO worksheet template. Can someone from Redwood put together a short response matrix (TTFT numbers under concurrency profiles + recommended mode and fallback)? We’d like it before our infra sync on Friday.

Best,
Tom
Senior Product, EdgePlay

Attachments: edgeplay-slo-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx), sample-payload-trace.json (json)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-06-27T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid response SLOs and streaming cadence — measurement plan

Looping in my quick measurement plan — I’ll run microbenchmarks against the hosted stack and a Dedicated-like replica. Plan:

- Payloads: use their sample (short prompts, 40–60 tokens typical) + synthetic long-tail payloads to surface tokenization variance.
- Concurrency shapes: 1, 10, 50 (steady-state), and 50->150 spike to simulate burst routing/fallbacks.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 TTFT, throughput (tokens/s), error rates, connection setup time (WS handshake vs SSE handshake) and per-chunk latency.
- Chunk cadence probe: emit with 100ms, 200ms, 400ms cadences; also test bundle-by-token vs bundle-by-time windows.
- Quantization test: FP16 baseline vs 4-bit quantized variant on same hardware; compare TTFT and a small quality holdout (5 prompts).

Expected outcomes by Thursday EOD: a CSV of measured latencies, a short recommendation (hosted + config vs Dedicated), and suggested fallbacks (model variants + routing).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai

Cc: Danielle Reyes <danielle@finops.io>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T18:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rapid response SLOs and streaming cadence — post-demo checklist

Tom / Danielle — quick update: Ben and Karthik completed the first run (hosted environment, us-west region) and we have preliminary numbers attached. Top-line:

- Hosted baseline (short prompt <=64 tokens): p95 TTFT ~ 135ms at 50 concurrent steady sessions (single region), p99 ~ 220ms.
- WebSocket vs SSE: delta is small (~10–20ms) — handshake cost for WS shows on cold starts but steady-state stream emission is comparable.
- Chunk cadence: 100ms cadence increases token overhead by ~8–12% vs 300ms (more small writes) and raises observed per-hour token counts. UX delta looks positive for 100–200ms cadence but cost impact is non-linear with frequent tiny chunks.
- Quantization: 4-bit variant reduced TTFT by ~20–30ms p95 but showed small regressions on 2/5 quality probes (we’ll include examples).

Actions for Friday infra sync (owners):
- Share the CSV + run logs (Ben) — link: https://drive.redwood/Shared/EdgePlay/SLO-worksheet
- Provide a recommended mode/config for lowest cost while meeting p95 <=150ms (Karthik)
- Draft fallback policy: prefer hosted FP16; fall back to quantized model only if cost threshold crossed, not for latency reasons (Ben + Karthik).

If that aligns, I’ll mark the worksheet as ready and we can sync with your infra team Friday 10am PT.

Thanks —
Chloe
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
